title: Tectonic hazards
examples: What causes the plates to move?
How do we predict a big earthquake?
What are the differences between a HIC and a LIC in relation to hazards?

explain.say: Today we are learning about tectonic hazards on Earth.

items: Earth's Crust: The rigid outer layer
Mantle: The hot, semi-solid layer below

explain.say: The Earth's surface is broken into large pieces called plates.

draw.text: Plates move due to convection currents

explain.say: These plates interact at their boundaries in three main ways.
A concrete example is the Mid-Atlantic Ridge spreading apart.
The effects include earthquakes and volcanic activity at these boundaries.

items: Earthquakes: Shaking from sudden release of energy
Volcanoes: Release of molten rock material

explain.say: In a real life example, the 2011 Tohoku earthquake showed these forces.

faq.q: What is the difference between an earthquake and a volcano?
faq.a: An earthquake is shaking caused by sudden movement along a fault. A volcano is an opening from which lava and ash erupt.
asks: Are they both related to plates?
What causes the shaking versus the eruption?

faq.q: Do all plate boundaries cause earthquakes?
faq.a: No, while most boundaries cause them, the specific type of movement dictates the intensity and location of the shaking.
asks: Can I have an earthquake far from a boundary?
Is it only at the edges of plates?

faq.q: How do we know if a region is prone to hazards?
faq.a: Geologists study historical records and current plate movement patterns to assess risk levels.

faq.q: What is the difference between HIC and LIC responses?
faq.a: HIC countries usually have better infrastructure for warning and recovery. LIC countries often face greater challenges in immediate response.
asks: What support do poor countries need?

faq.q: Can we predict the exact time of the next big earthquake?
faq.a: Currently, scientists cannot predict the exact time or location of a major earthquake with certainty.
asks: Will we ever know when it will strike?
Is there a warning system for time?

facts: Plate boundaries are areas where the Earth's crust plates meet.
Divergent boundaries create new crustal material.
Convergent boundaries can cause subduction, where one plate slides under another.
Tsunamis are large waves often caused by underwater earthquakes.

quiz.say: If two plates are moving towards each other, what type of boundary is this?
quiz.why: When plates move together, they collide, which is a convergent boundary.

wrong.0: This happens when plates pull apart, not when they crash.
wrong.1: This boundary involves plates sliding sideways past each other.
wrong.2: This is not a recognized type of plate boundary interaction.

quiz.say: What is the primary process causing the movement of the tectonic plates?
quiz.why: Heat transfer through the movement of material in the mantle drives the plates.

wrong.0: Wind patterns affect the atmosphere, not the solid plates beneath us.
wrong.2: Tidal forces are caused by the moon and sun's gravity.
wrong.3: While rotation exists, it is not the main driver of plate movement.

quiz.say: A community with advanced warning systems and strong building codes is more likely to be:
quiz.why: HIC stands for High Income Country, which usually means better resources for response.

wrong.0: LIC stands for Low Income Country, which often has fewer resources.
wrong.1: This term is too general and does not describe resource capacity.
wrong.2: This is a subjective term and not the geographical classification used.
